subject: porbeagle shark
title: A Shark's Tracking Tag Turned Warm Because a Bigger Shark Ate It

scenes.text: A shark's tracking tag suddenly got warm, deep underwater.
Scientists had tagged a pregnant, seven-foot porbeagle shark off Cape Cod.
For five months, the tag logged normal dives into cold, dark water.
Then, even six hundred metres down, it read a steady seventy-two degrees Fahrenheit, for four days.
That's body heat. The tag was inside something bigger, most likely a great white over fifteen feet long.
The scientists weren't tracking a shark anymore. They were tracking its killer's stomach.

description:
A pop-off tag on a pregnant 2.2-metre porbeagle shark tagged off Cape Cod recorded normal dives for five months, then a steady temperature of about 22 C even at depths of 150 to 600 metres for four days.
Researchers concluded it had been eaten by a warm-bodied predator, most likely a large white shark, the first recorded predation on a porbeagle.
Which shark do you think did it?
first_comment: The tag finally floated up near Bermuda, 158 days after it was attached. A shortfin mako was the other suspect. Great white or mako?
